newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks regional CIC plans by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: France seeks regional CIC plans by yr-end.

text.p: Finance Minister Jean Arthuis has asked the regional heads of the French CIC group of 11 banks to draw up new proposals by the year-end on privatising CIC, budget minister Alain Lamassoure said on Tuesday.

"The finance minister met the heads of all the CIC regional subsidiaries and has asked them to produce fresh proposals by the year-end on a new way to privatise CIC so that the unity of the group and employment can be fully guaranteed," Lamassoure told the lower house National Assembly.

The government said last week that it had scrapped a tender to privatise CIC after getting just one eligible bid, from BNP , and has since then called for the resignation of CIC's state parent company GAN chairman, Jean-Jacques Bonnaud.
"The privatisation will be taken up again on a new basis," said Lamassoure, who elaborated on the government's discontent with GAN head Bonnaud and CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt.

"We have to draw the consequences as far as the management of GAN, CIC's owner, is concerned. The experience has shown that privatisation can only succeed if it has the full backing and cooperation of the managers concerned," he said.
Whoever replaces Bonnaud will name a new chairman at CIC in the place of chairman Bernard Yoncourt, government sources say.
Arthuis, who returns from Japan on Thursday, said last week he was abandoning a CIC privatisation tender which attracted only the BNP but that he was determined to privatise the group.
Bonnaud is resisting the government call on Monday for his dismissal and faces being fired by government decree next week if he refuses to back down.
